entries.proposition: Baseline difference that decides what a wild-type arm can show: wild-type mice have almost no SWDs per day (11.7 versus 1723 in the mutant), so a drug effect on SWD count in wild type is bounded at the floor. A mutant-only suppression on this endpoint is guaranteed by the baseline and is not evidence of a genotype-dependent drug action.
entries.snippet: while WT mice exhibited extremely rare SWDs (Figures 2B, C; mean ± SEM WT: 11.7 ± 6.5) in a 24 h period.
entries.anchor: Results, Excitability phenotypes in Gnb1K78R/+ mice

entries.proposition: Both valproate and ethosuximide nearly abolished SWDs in the mutant after acute treatment, with recovery within about one to one and a half hours; phenytoin did not reduce SWDs. Valproate is described in the Discussion as not inhibiting GIRK or T-type channels, so a drug that does neither also abolished the SWDs.
entries.snippet: Acute treatment of Gnb1K78R/+ mice with either ETX or VPA nearly abolished SWDs (Figure 4A).
entries.anchor: Results, Ethosuximide corrects EEG and network firing patterns

Stars mark mutant versus wild type at pre, 1 h and 1.5 h; the 30 min point is circled with no star. Valproate panel is the same shape from about 31 to about 2.5; phenytoin panel stays high (about 40 rising to about 64) in the mutant with wild type at 0. entries.proposition: The authors write that, together, their considerations support the hypothesis that, in countering the variant-related spike-wave discharges, ethosuximide acts on a target other than both sodium channels and T-type calcium channels.
entries.snippet: Together, these considerations support the hypothesis that, in countering GNB1 K78R-related SWDs, ETX acts on a target other than both Na+ channels and T-type Ca2+ channels.

entries.proposition: Controversy statement in the paper's own words: ethosuximide is thought to act mainly as a T-type blocker, but the extent of T-type block at physiologically relevant concentrations is disputed.
entries.snippet: ETX is thought to act mainly as a T-type Ca2+ channel blocker (Coulter et al., 1989), although controversy remains as to the extent of this block at physiologically relevant doses of ETX (Gomora et al., 2001; Crunelli and Leresche, 2002; Tringham et al., 2012).

entries.proposition: Methods mention Cav3.2 currents measured by two-electrode voltage clamp in oocytes, but on the body surface (Results and every figure legend) no Cav3.2 result is reported; the supplementary PDF was not opened, so the absence is a statement about the body only.
entries.snippet: Whole-cell GIRK and Cav3.2 currents in oocytes were measured using a two-electrode voltage clamp (TEVC) with Geneclamp 500 (Molecular Devices)
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, Electrophysiology in oocytes

entries.proposition: Ethosuximide inhibits Gβγ-activated GIRK2 at far lower concentration than basal GIRK1/2 in oocytes: EC50 about 55 micromolar versus about 1.5 to 2 millimolar. The GIRK1/2 value lies at or above the top of the range the paper calls therapeutic, so how much GIRK block occurs at therapeutic exposure depends on the channel composition in the cell, which the paper says is unknown.
entries.snippet: Remarkably, Gβγ-activated GIRK2 was inhibited at much lower doses (Figures 7A–C), with an EC50 of ~55 μM (Figure 7 and Supplementary Figures 6A, B).
entries.anchor: Results, Ethosuximide differentially inhibits GIRK1/2 and GIRK2 channels

entries.proposition: Figure 7B read as an image: Gβγ-activated GIRK2 inhibition curves cross 50 percent at about 0.03 to 0.06 millimolar for both wild-type and K78R Gβ, inside the shaded therapeutic range; GIRK1/2 without Gβγ crosses 50 percent at about 2 to 3 millimolar, to the right of the shaded range. Wild-type and K78R curves are similar or K78R slightly left: ethosuximide's GIRK block is not mutant-specific in the oocyte, so any genotype dependence must come from the larger Gβγ-driven GIRK current in the mutant cell.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 7B: GIRK2+GβK78R curve (orange squares) 50 percent near 0.03 mM; GIRK2+GβWT (blue) near 0.06 mM; GIRK1/2 (black) near 2 to 3 mM; shaded band about 0.25 to 0.9 mM.
entries.anchor: Figure 7 panel B, page 17 embedded raster 1772x1206

entries.proposition: Null-like and missense genotypes differ: heterozygous Gnb1 deletion (haploinsufficiency) did not lower the electroconvulsive threshold while the K78R missense did. A drug effect or a seizure phenotype in a missense or gain-of-function allele cannot be assumed for a null allele of the same gene, and the converse holds for WWOX.
entries.snippet: Female and male Gnb1Del71/+ mice showed ECT values equivalent to WT controls (Figure 2A), demonstrating that Gnb1 haploinsufficiency does not lead to enhanced seizure susceptibility.
entries.anchor: Results, Excitability phenotypes in Gnb1K78R/+ mice

entries.proposition: The authors report that, at the lowest of three tested ethosuximide concentrations, the drug did not affect the bursting phenotype of the mutant cultured networks, at the middle concentration it restored close-to-normal firing, and that the highest concentration seemed to produce an overshoot effect and greatly reduced network activity.
entries.snippet: At 250 μM, ETX did not affect the bursting phenotype, while at 750 μM, ETX did restore close-to-normal firing to the mutant network. ETX increased number of bursts per minute, decreased mean duration of bursts, and decreased IBIs, compared to the vehicle or 250 μM-treated Gnb1K78R/+ networks. Interestingly, 2 mM ETX seemed to produce an “overshoot” effect and greatly reduced the network activity.
entries.anchor: Results, Ethosuximide corrects EEG and network firing patterns

entries.proposition: Figure 3 read as an image (microelectrode arrays of cultured cortical neurons): the heterozygous cultures fire bursts less often (about 4.4 to 5 against 5.5 to 6.8 per minute; P = 2.4e-13), with longer bursts (about 1.1 to 1.5 against 0.9 to 1.2 s) and more spikes per burst (about 54 to 66 against 43 to 48) while the mean firing rate differs little (P = 0.029) and spike frequency in bursts is similar.

entries.proposition: Figure 5 read as an image (baclofen-evoked whole-cell currents): hippocampal excitatory neurons show larger currents in the heterozygous mice at the middle and highest concentrations (about 0.11 against 0.05 pA/pF, three stars; about 0.29 against 0.20, one star), hippocampal inhibitory neurons larger at both (about 0.10 against 0.05, two stars; about 0.28 against 0.09, three stars), cortical inhibitory neurons larger at the highest only (about 0.28 against 0.20, one star) and cortical excitatory neurons not different.

entries.proposition: Figure 6 read as an image (oocyte co-expression): with GIRK1/2 the variant Gbeta gives more current than wild type at low RNA doses (about 6.6 against 4.1 microamp at 0.1 ng; stars) and less at the highest dose (about 4.7 against 9.4 at 5 ng; four stars) although more protein reaches the membrane; with GIRK2 alone the variant gives more current at 0.5 and 1 ng (about 2.3 against 0.15 and 3.8 against 1.2 microamp; four stars) and less at 5 ng (about 2.5 against 3.4).
